editorial:
Imagine stepping back into 2002 when pop music ruled the airwaves and girl groups were everything. You get to experience the magic of Britain's biggest stars, Atomic Kitten, during their very first U.K. tour. The vibe is pure energy and nostalgia as Natasha, Lil, and Jenny take over the stage at Belfast's Waterfront. From the second they hit the first note of Right Now, you can feel the excitement of the capacity crowd. It feels less like a movie and more like you have a front-row ticket to a massive party, complete with flashy lights and great outfits.

What really makes this stand out is how it captures the raw energy of a live show. You will love the synchronized dance moves with their male dancers and the way the Phat Cats backing band keeps the beat pumping. While it is a straightforward concert film without a complex plot, the pacing is fast and the hits keep coming. If you want to relive the early 2000s, you should definitely try streaming this in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best quality.
endingExplained: The show wraps up with the group performing their biggest chart-topping hits to a cheering crowd. After a series of costume changes and high-energy dance numbers, the girls thank their fans for all the support during their first tour. The film ends on a high note with a final spectacular performance that leaves the audience wanting more, showing the group at the peak of their fame before the curtain finally closes.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves early 2000s pop music and girl groups.
